data.description:
## Context / Problem

Both engines must produce the same verdict contract, so downstream readers (claim gate, `review-plan --status`, `sign-review`, MCP status tools, the sidecar readers) need no change and the two engines are directly comparable. The pipeline's verdict is built by `orchestrator.finalize_verdict` (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/orchestrator.py:333`) and recorded by `sidecar.build_payload`/`sidecar.emit` (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sidecar.py:586`, `:58`) against `src/rebar/schemas/plan_review_verdict.schema.json` and `review_result.schema.json`. The agentic engine returns a different finding shape.

## Approach

Add an adapter in the agentic module's package (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/agentic_verdict.py`) that maps agentic findings onto the pipeline's finding and verdict shape, per ADR 0123:

- `severity == "blocker"` goes to `blocking`; `major`, `minor` and `trivial` go to `advisory` (operator decision on the epic, 2026-11-09). Zero blockers is PASS.
- Field mapping: `title` + `description` become the finding text, `evidence` the evidence list, `suggested_fix` the remediation, `criterion` the criteria list (`general` when absent), `severity` is kept as an attribute; finding ids are minted with `orchestrator.mint_finding_id` (`orchestrator.py:105`) so dedup and prior-concern matching work unchanged.
- A runner error or malformed output becomes INDETERMINATE with the same `resolution_class` the pipeline uses for a failed LLM pass, so `attest.sign_plan_review` (`attest.py:113`) refuses to sign it exactly as it refuses a degraded pipeline verdict.
- Coverage records `engine: "agentic"` and the model that ran.

The adapted verdict then flows through the unchanged post-dispatch path in `_run_plan_review` (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py`, after `produce_plan_review_verdict`): Pass-3 floors, advisory cap, sidecar emit and signing. Mapping at the engine boundary, rather than teaching each reader a second shape, is what keeps every downstream reader untouched.

## Scope

- src/rebar/llm/plan_review/agentic_verdict.py (new)
- src/rebar/llm/plan_review/agentic.py (call the adapter)
- tests/unit/test_plan_review_agentic_verdict.py (new)
- tests/unit/test_plan_review_verdict_schema_parity.py (new: both engines against the same schemas)

## Testing

- Worked example: findings `[{severity: "blocker", ...}, {severity: "major", ...}]` produce `verdict: BLOCK` with one `blocking` and one `advisory` entry; `[{severity: "major"}, {severity: "trivial"}]` produce PASS with two advisory entries; `[]` produces PASS with none.
- Failure/edge: runner error and schema-invalid output produce INDETERMINATE that `sign_plan_review` refuses; an unknown severity value is treated as advisory and logged, never as blocking by default.
- Schema parity: a pipeline verdict from `FakeRunner` and an agentic verdict both validate against `plan_review_verdict.schema.json`, and both sidecar payloads validate against `review_result.schema.json`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The severity-to-verdict and field mappings above are pinned by `tests/unit/test_plan_review_agentic_verdict.py`.
- [ ] Both engines' verdicts and sidecars validate against the same schemas, pinned by `tests/unit/test_plan_review_verdict_schema_parity.py`.
- [ ] `make verify` exits 0.
data.title: Agentic verdict adapter: map agent findings onto the plan_review_verdict and REVIEW_RESULT schemas
